title: RFC 9338 Countersign_structure (to-be-signed array)
description: DERIVED - not verbatim. RFC 9338 ships CDDL, not JSON Schema; this is this library's machine-checkable rendering of section 3.3's Countersign_structure, written against the CDDL in countersign-structure.derived.cddl with erratum 7338 applied. It models the DECODED array, with byte strings as lowercase hex strings, because JSON Schema has no byte-string type. The arity rules that CDDL cannot state - which context string goes with which presence of other_fields - are encoded here as a oneOf, which is more than the source states in one place and is derived from section 3.3's four context bullets.

oneOf.title: full countersignature, other_fields absent (COSE_Signature, COSE_Sign, COSE_Encrypt, COSE_Encrypt0, COSE_recipient)
full countersignature, other_fields present (COSE_Sign1, COSE_Mac, COSE_Mac0)
abbreviated countersignature, other_fields absent; sign_protected omitted
abbreviated countersignature, other_fields present; sign_protected omitted

bstr.description: a CBOR byte string, lowercase hex, possibly empty

other_fields.description: RFC 9338 section 3.3: "This field is an array of all bstr fields after the second." of the target structure. Derived from RFC 9052's CDDL, this is [signature] for COSE_Sign1 and [tag] for COSE_Mac and COSE_Mac0, and the field is absent for every other permitted target. See bstr-slot-census.derived.txt.

x-derived-notes: WHERE THIS IS STRICTER THAN THE SOURCE. The oneOf pairs each context string with an arity. RFC 9338 states the pairing as four prose bullets and does not restate it in its CDDL, whose `context` is a free choice of the four strings with `? other_fields` independent - so the source's own grammar admits the context string "CounterSignature" WITH other_fields and "CounterSignatureV2" WITHOUT, both of which section 3.3's prose forbids.

WHERE THIS IS LOOSER THAN THE SOURCE. It cannot express that body_protected and payload are drawn from the target structure, nor the section 3.3 precondition that the target's cryptographic functions are finalized first. Those are requirements, not shapes: rfc-9338#R-0093, rfc-9338#R-0096, rfc-9338#R-0086.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DECIDE. section 3.3 does not say what fills `payload` when the target has no payload field (COSE_Signature, COSE_Encrypt, COSE_Encrypt0, COSE_recipient). This schema therefore constrains `payload` only to be a byte string. See ../design-notes.md section 3.
